author: Gaohan123
body:
[P1] Scope the receive consensus to the TP group

This consensus must only include ranks that jointly execute the same TP-sharded request. `pt.world` also contains DP/PP ranks, while the `LOCAL` role currently only excludes CFG/SP topologies. In TP+DP execution, different DP replicas can process different request IDs, so this code mixes receive flags from unrelated requests; a miss in one replica unnecessarily invalidates another request. More seriously, if one replica skips the exchange—for example because it is handling a dummy or invalid request—while another enters it, the world-group send/broadcast sequence can deadlock.

Please use the tensor-parallel group (for example, `get_tp_group()`) for this exchange and add a TP=2, DP=2 test where the two DP replicas handle different request IDs and receive outcomes.

author: Gaohan123
body:
[P1] Include CFG companion KV results in the consensus verdict

At this point, `received` only represents the primary KV result: `receive_multi_kv_cache()` returns `primary_ok` even when one or more `cfg_kv_collect_func` companion receives fail. Bagel's collector reports such failures by returning a partial dictionary, so all ranks can report `received=True` while only some ranks have `cfg_text` or `cfg_img` KV. Those TP ranks then continue with different branch caches and potentially different cache lengths, producing inconsistent TP-sharded computation and possibly another collective mismatch.

This is relevant to the failing Bagel test because it supplies a negative prompt and therefore creates a `cfg_text` companion request. Please make the consensus cover every expected companion role as well as the primary KV, and clear the complete payload on all TP ranks if any required role is missing on any rank. A regression test should cover primary success on every rank with a companion timeout on one rank.

author: tzhouam
body:
Good catch — agreed on both counts, and the deadlock half was the serious one: a DP replica skipping the exchange on a dummy request while another entered it would hang the world group. Fixed in bac3eafc:

- `_TransferTopoConfig` now carries the stage's tensor-model-parallel group (`vllm.distributed.parallel_state.get_tp_group()`, `None` when vLLM TP isn't initialized) and the consensus runs exclusively on it; `pt.world` is never touched by the exchange. Within the TP group every skip guard (topology, `need_recv_cache`, dummy-request id) is symmetric, since all TP ranks execute the same request.
- Tests: `test_world_group_is_never_used_for_the_exchange` models the TP=2×DP=2 layout you described (world of 4, TP group of 2) and asserts the exchange happens on the TP group with world receiving zero calls; the existing rank-role tests were moved onto the TP group. A true multi-process TP×DP e2e isn't in CI's current matrix, but the deadlock precondition — asymmetric entry into the exchange — is now structurally impossible because no guard depends on state that can differ within the TP group.

Local `test_bagel[tp_vae_patch_parallel_2]` e2e re-passed on the updated code (9 min, L20X×2, vLLM 0.26).

author: tzhouam
body:
Confirmed — `receive_multi_kv_cache` returns `primary_ok` only and companion collection is best-effort (partial dicts applied, exceptions swallowed), so ranks could agree on `received=True` while diverging on `cfg_text`/`cfg_img`. Fixed in bac3eafc:

- Ranks now exchange a state signature instead of a flag: `(primary_received, tuple(sorted(_collect_request_kv_payload(req))))`. Reusing `_collect_request_kv_payload` means the signature automatically tracks every applied role — primary, metadata, and all `cfg_*` branch fields — with no separate role list to maintain. Verdict is "identical signature on every TP rank"; any divergence clears the full payload everywhere (via the same enumeration) and falls back together.
- One deliberate deviation from "clear if any required role is missing on any rank": if a role is missing on *all* ranks symmetrically, the state is kept. Symmetric absence is consistent — for `cfg_text` it's Bagel's documented empty-unconditional-branch path (original BAGEL text2img behavior) — so failing it would degrade requests that succeed today. Only cross-rank *divergence* can desync collectives, and that's exactly what the signature comparison rejects. Happy to tighten to strict completeness if you see a case symmetric absence breaks.
- Tests: `test_rank0_drops_kv_on_companion_role_divergence` (primary OK everywhere, `cfg_text` on one rank only → cleared on all) and `test_rank0_keeps_symmetric_partial_state`.

Live validation: in the local e2e rerun of `test_bagel[tp_vae_patch_parallel_2]` (which sends a negative prompt, so `cfg_text` is exercised), the new path caught a real divergence — rank 0 reported `['kv_metadata', 'past_key_values', 'sp.cfg_kv_request_ids', ...]`, rank 1 only `['sp.cfg_kv_request_ids']` — both ranks dropped and fell back together, and the test passed.
